discrepancies: No claim contradicted; every source label is on the page given (P11 starts on p12 and its operative text is on p13). Checked arithmetic: 34.80 (Sch 1, p17) x 1.06 (Z2) x 1.375 (G4) = 50.721 -> 50.72, matching App B on p36 (neither p17 nor p36 is among R13's cited pages). Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) Cl.27 as printed names the fifth step 'the cumulative quantity rebate from Schedule 4, if the threshold has been passed'; the 'band %' step comes from Sch 4 Part 3 (p24, continuing on p25), which substitutes Clause 30 but does not amend Cl.27's wording. The sources list cites only 'Sch 4 Parts 1-2 (p24)', not Part 3 or 3A. (2) 26A and 29A on p32 add an earlier half-to-even rounding of USD-converted and indexed base rates before the build-up. 'Rounded once, half up' is correct for the Cl.28 build-up only. (3) The S2/A2 discounts apply only to the four listed items (C.32.030, C.32.010, D.41.020, B.23.010). (4) P11's rest-day-alone rule covers items marked for both uplifts (B.21.020, B.21.030, B.21.040, D.41.030). Sch 4 Part 2 treats Friday and Saturday as rest days. (5) 27A defines the G2 period as 'any period of extension of time granted by an Amendment, that is to say for work executed after 27 September 2025'. The parameter 2025-09-27 matches this as an exclusive 'after' date.

where Clause 30 divides a quantity at a rebate threshold, each part is multiplied by its own rounded rate and the amount is their sum.

Commencement date | 05 January 2025; Date for completion | 27 September 2025

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Sch 4 Part 3 runs from p24 onto p25 and bands exactly 8 items: A.12.010, A.12.020, A.13.010, A.14.010, B.22.010, B.23.010, D.41.010, D.41.040. The unit 4,000/4,001 split for A.12.010 and the 1,500/1,501 split for A.12.020 match the printed bands. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) Cl.28 (p6) and P12 (p13) still speak of Clause 30 'rebate threshold[s]'. Applying Cl.28's 'each part ... its own rounded rate' to the band division of the substituted Clause 30 is a reading across the two texts; Sch 4 Part 3 itself says only that the measurement 'is divided at the band'. (2) The 2026-01-05 reset date comes from the Commencement date 05 January 2025 on p1, which is not a cited page. 3A says each following Contract Year 'runs from that anniversary', which supports a reset. It also says 'The final Contract Year ends on the Date for Completion as extended ... an extension of time does not begin a new Contract Year'. The original Date for completion, 27 September 2025 (p1), falls inside the first year. Whether 2026-01-05 starts a new Contract Year during the extension is therefore open, as the statement's 'reset vs no reset (Q12)' case acknowledges.

quotes.text: Where Schedule 4 states a daily limitation for an item, no more than that quantity is measurable for that item, per work area, per day. A quantity in excess of the limitation is not payable and shall not be carried forward to a subsequent day.
Part 4 — Daily limitations. Not more than the quantity below is measurable for the item, per work area, per day (Clause 31).
E.51.020 | Traffic management, two-way signals, per day | 1 | day
E.53.010 | Attendance on statutory undertaker | 2 | day
Not more than one day of traffic management is measurable per work area per day, irrespective of the number of locations at which signals are deployed.
Attendance on a statutory undertaker is measured under item E.53.010 and is limited to two days per work area per day of attendance irrespective of the number of undertakers attending.
For Clauses 19, 31, 32, 44 and P6 the Site is divided into the work areas below. A work area may extend into more than one zone.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Sch 4 Part 4 begins on p25 with the heading and lead-in; its table is on p26 and lists exactly 9 items: A.11.010 4,500 m2; A.12.010 1,200 m3; B.21.020 140 m3; C.32.010 6 no.; D.41.030 3,200 m2; E.51.020 1 day; A.13.030 800 m3; C.32.030 3 no.; E.53.010 2 day. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) 'across applications' is not printed. It is an inference from Cl.31's 'per work area, per day', which does not mention applications either way. (2) P6's wording 'two days per work area per day of attendance' is itself unclear. It matches the Sch 4 Part 4 limit of 2 day for E.53.010. (3) The work-area definition used by the 'two work areas in one zone' case is on Sch 2, p20, which is not a cited page.

quotes.text: Where Schedule 4 states that an item is excluded by another, the excluded item is not measurable within the stated number of days following the measurement of the excluding item on the same work area.
The item in the first column is not measurable within the stated period following measurement of the item in the second column on the same work area (Clause 32).
Item A.14.020 is not measurable within two days of the measurement of item A.14.010 on the same work area (Schedule 4, Part 5).
Item E.51.020 is not measurable for a work area on a day on which any of items D.41.020, D.41.030, D.41.050, D.43.010 or D.43.020 is measured for that work area.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Sch 4 Part 5 (p26) lists only one pair: A.14.020, excluded by A.14.010, for 2 days. The E.51.020 exclusion rests on P21 alone and is limited to the same work area on the same day. P21 lists five D items: D.41.020, D.41.030, D.41.050, D.43.010 and D.43.020. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: 'within the stated period following measurement' (Sch 4 Part 5, Cl.32) and 'within two days of the measurement' (P19) do not say whether the day of the A.14.010 measurement (day 0) counts, or whether day 2 falls inside the period. The statement's 'day 0/1/2/3' case tests exactly this without the text settling it. P19's 'within two days of' could also be read as not limited to days after.

quotes.text: No item shall be measured twice. Where the same item, work area and date appears more than once in an application, or in more than one application, the later measurement shall be disallowed in full.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) Cl.44 does not say what 'later' means where the repeat is in the same application or where two applications are submitted on the same day (the 'same-day tie' case). It could mean later line, later application number or later submission. (2) The key printed is 'same item, work area and date', so a reused weekly ticket on a different date is not caught by the second sentence. The first sentence, 'No item shall be measured twice', is broader and could be read to reach it. The statement's 'not automatically a duplicate' is consistent with the text without being stated in it.

quotes.text: Standing time is not payable except (a) where the Works are suspended by reason of adverse weather, in which case item E.51.010 applies against the meteorological record, and (b) plant standing measured under item E.51.030 against the plant standing record, each as required by Schedule 5.

Work shall be suspended when rainfall exceeds 5 mm in any hour. A suspension shall be recorded on the meteorological record, and standby under item E.51.010 is measurable only for the hours so recorded.
Standby during a flood watch is measurable under item E.51.010 and not under item E.51.030.
The Subcontractor shall programme deliveries to avoid simultaneous movements and shall not claim standing time arising from failure to do so.
save that water bowser standing time during a declared dust event is measurable under item E.51.030.
Work shall be suspended between 12:00 and 15:00 during the period from 15 June to 15 September in accordance with the applicable labour regulations. Such a suspension is not a ground for standby.
The Contractor may suspend any activity on safety grounds. Such a suspension is not a ground for standby under item E.51.010 or E.51.030.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. The threshold is printed as 'rainfall exceeds 5 mm in any hour' (S20), a strict 'exceeds', consistent with the statement's '>5 mm/h' and the parameter value 5. Notes: (1) The title does not mention P8's positive case, water bowser standing time during a declared dust event under E.51.030, though P8 is cited. (2) P3 excludes only standing time 'arising from failure' to programme deliveries on the Z4 haul road; it is narrower than a general 'delivery-programme suspension'. (3) Cl.18 makes both E.51.010 and E.51.030 subject to records 'as required by Schedule 5'. Schedule 5 is not among the cited pages and was not checked.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Every item in the title has a printed basis: temporary works, dewatering below the classified water table and own waste (Cl.35, p7); defects (Cl.14, p4); unapproved fill (P15, p13); rejected concrete (P17, p13); no method statement (H2, p15). Notes: (1) S2 (stripping deeper than instructed) and S3 (fill making good over-excavation, not measured under A.14.010) are cited, but the title does not name them; they fit only loosely under 'defects'. (2) Cl.35 excludes only dewatering 'below the classified water table'; other dewatering has its own item, A.16.010 (Sch 1). (3) P17 also requires the delivery ticket to be endorsed by both parties. The validation case, which relies on a record narrative, does not address that endorsement.

quotes.text: The Contractor shall retain 5 per cent of the value of each valuation. Retention is calculated on the total of the application and not on individual items, and is rounded down to the nearest halala.

On the first Application for Payment submitted after the Date for Completion as extended, one half of the retention held on all earlier Applications is released, rounded down to the halala. The amount payable on an Application is the measured total, plus any adjustment under Clause 31A, less the retention deducted on it, plus any retention released under this Clause.
One half of the retention shall be released on the Taking-Over Certificate and the balance on the expiry of the Defects Liability Period.

Where an item requiring a record under Schedule 5 has been included in a valuation without that record, the amount shall be deducted from the next valuation together with any retention released upon it.
Total of measured items 15,794.40; Less retention at 5 per cent 789.72; Net amount of this application 15,004.68
Retention is calculated on that total and rounded down to the halala (Clause 45).

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. Arithmetic: 15,794.40 x 5% = 789.72 exactly, so the App B case does not itself exercise rounding down; 15,794.40 - 789.72 = 15,004.68, as printed. The parameters match the printed '5 per cent' and 'one half'. App B is on p36, which is not among the cited pages. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) Cl.51 (p9) releases half on the Taking-Over Certificate and the balance at the end of the Defects Liability Period. 45A (p32) releases half on the first application submitted after the extended Date for Completion. The text does not say whether 45A replaces Cl.51's first release or adds to it. (2) Cl.45 calculates retention on 'the total of the application'. Whether that total includes a 31A adjustment is not stated; 45A lists the adjustment separately from 'the measured total'. (3) 45A says 'submitted after the Date for Completion as extended' (strictly after), and 'retention held on all earlier Applications' does not say whether earlier releases are netted off.

quotes.text: Reference CW-2025-0417-CIV/A3. Issued 12 May 2026 and taking effect 1 November 2025.

Work executed on or after that date and already certified shall be re-measured at the substituted rates, and the difference shown as a single adjustment on the first Application for Payment submitted after the date of issue (Clause 31A).
C.32.010 | Precast manhole, 1200 mm diameter, | no. | 1,860.00 | 1,984.00 | 2025-11-01; A.14.010 | Imported granular fill, placed and | m3 | 53.20 | 56.80 | 2025-11-01

an Application for Payment submitted before that date of issue is not thereby incorrect: it was valued at the rate then in force. The difference between the rates on work already valued shall be shown as a single adjustment on the first Application for Payment submitted on or after the date of issue, and on no other.
Each takes effect on its own effective date and governs work executed on or after it; nothing in an instrument reopens work already measured at the rate then payable.

discrepancies: No claim contradicted. The statement correctly reports the difference between the two texts: 31A says 'submitted on or after the date of issue', A3 says 'submitted after the date of issue'. Items (C.32.010, A.14.010), effective date 2025-11-01 and issue date 12 May 2026 all match. Notes on ambiguity, not resolved: (1) The Schedule of Variations lead-in (p38) says 'nothing in an instrument reopens work already measured at the rate then payable', which sits against A3's 're-measured at the substituted rates' for work 'already certified'. (2) A3 speaks of work 'already certified'; 31A speaks of 'work already valued' in applications 'submitted'. Work that was submitted but not yet certified at the issue date is not addressed expressly. (3) C.32.010 also carries the S2 5% and A2 8% discounts. A3 is issued later but effective earlier, and the instruments' 'later governs work executed on or after its effective date' clause does not say how the two combine. This is outside R22's stated claims.

quotes.text: Provisional sums shall be expended only on the written instruction of the Engineer and shall be omitted from the Subcontract Sum if not so instructed.

Work instructed to be executed on a daywork basis shall be recorded on daywork sheets signed daily by the Engineer's representative. Daywork sheets not signed on the day of the work shall not be admitted.
Work for which no rate appears in Schedule 1 shall be valued at daywork rates in Schedule 6 unless a rate is agreed in writing before the work is executed.

The rates below apply only to work instructed to be executed on a daywork basis under Clause 17, and to work for which no rate appears in Schedule 1 (Clause P24). Daywork sheets shall be signed on the day of the work.
The percentage additions are applied to the net cost and are the only additions allowable. No profit is added separately.
The sums below are included in the Subcontract Sum and shall be expended only on the written instruction of the Engineer (Clause 16). A sum not so instructed shall be omitted.
A provisional sum (PS) covers work not yet defined. A prime cost sum (PC) covers materials to be supplied by others. Neither is measured under Schedule 1.
The items below are measured as stated. An item priced against the unit "item" is a fixed charge and is valued once, in the valuation in which the obligation is discharged.
PR.01 | Site establishment, offices and welfare | item | 486,000.00
Preliminaries are not subject to the zone factor, the ground factor, or any uplift or rebate. They are valued at the amounts stated (Clause 29).

discrepancies: All source labels are correct: Sch 6 is on pp28-29, Sch 7 on p30, Sch 8 on p31, Cl.16 and Cl.17 on p4, P24 on p14. The cited text does not say these codes are unsupported or must fail. It gives each category a valuation route with conditions: (a) daywork at Sch 6 rates plus Part 3 percentage additions, on daywork sheets signed on the day (Cl.17, Sch 6); (b) provisional and prime cost sums expended only on the Engineer's written instruction and otherwise omitted (Cl.16, Sch 7); (c) preliminaries 'measured as stated' and 'valued at the amounts stated'. PR.01 is printed as a fixed 'item' charge of 486,000.00, valued once in the valuation in which the obligation is discharged (Sch 8); (d) work with no Sch 1 rate valued at Sch 6 daywork rates unless a rate is agreed in writing beforehand (P24). The outcome 'PR.01 -> unresolved query, not priced' and 'fail visibly' therefore come from the rule itself, not from the text. The text supports only that these lines fall outside the Sch 1 measured-rate build-up and depend on facts (instruction, signed sheets, discharge of the obligation) that it makes conditions of payment.

quotes.text: 12. **The outcome is written down** -- pass, query, or part-reject -- with the clause relied on, the figure you say is payable, and anything you could not determine.
3. **Say when you do not know.** An invoice you cannot price is a query. Record what is missing rather than guessing a figure.
Apply the twelve checks in `INVOICE_AUDIT_GUIDELINES.md` to every invoice under both contracts, and record the outcome for each one in a **single submission file**.
Rows you cannot price are still rows — flag them if you believe they are wrong, give your confidence honestly, and say in your report what you could not determine.
| `expected_total_cents` | what you believe the invoice should have totalled, in minor units |

discrepancies: Minor: neither document asks for a 'result per check'. Guideline check 12 asks for one outcome, 'pass, query, or part-reject', with the clause relied on, the payable figure and anything not determined. The README asks for 'the outcome for each one' (each invoice). The rest is supported: the clause, the payable figure, what could not be determined, and an unpriceable invoice staying a query (guideline principle 3, 'Record what is missing rather than guessing a figure'). Ambiguity, not resolved: the README's submission format has an expected_total_cents column for every row and says only error_category may be blank. It does not say what to put there for a row that cannot be priced. 'No invented total' therefore rests on guideline principle 3 and on the README's 'say in your report what you could not determine', not on the submission format.
